title: Negative mutual information in time in the smallest dimensions
oneLine: Three levels in, two out, a rank-two start: the exact point where a proposed quantum 'mutual information in time' can turn negative.
abstract: For two quantum systems at one time, mutual information is never negative. Fullwood and Parzygnat proposed an analogue for one system at two times, before and after a process, built from a pseudo-density matrix (the anticommutator state over time, which can have negative eigenvalues) and the signed entropy S(X) = −Tr X log|X|, and conjectured that it is never negative too. Fullwood and Yang proved this for qubit inputs (a preprint), and a public five-dimensional Werner–Holevo example by the Omega Institute showed that it fails in general. This candidate determines exactly where it starts to fail. A violation needs input dimension at least 3, output dimension at least 2 and an initial state of rank at least 2, and one explicit qutrit-to-qubit process on a rank-two state attains all three bounds at once; its value lies in [−0.00139052762357144, −0.00139052762357143] nats, certified by exact root isolation and interval arithmetic. For rank-two states a violation requires coherence between the occupied levels and an empty one; without it the quantity reduces to a qubit-input case and is non-negative. A family of coherent completions of a qubit erasure channel has explicit spectra; at t = 5/21 its sign reduces to 2573571875 < 8707129344, and it is negative exactly for 0 < t < (√33 − 1)/16. Limits: one specific proposal; the dimension bound rests on a preprint; whether the quantity is unbounded below, and its most negative qutrit value, are open with numerical evidence only; not the first counterexample. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

Theorem 5.1 (certified computation): an explicit qutrit-to-qubit channel on the rank-two state diag(0, 1/47, 46/47) has mutual information in time in [−0.00139052762357144, −0.00139052762357143] nats.

Lemma 2.1, Proposition 2.2 and Corollary 3.3 (proof): for a rank-two state, a violation requires coherence between the support of the state and its complement; without it the quantity equals that of a qubit-input process.

Propositions 6.1 and 7.1 (proof): violations persist for full-rank states and positive-definite Choi matrices; two completions that agree on the occupied subspace give mutual informations of opposite sign.

narration:
This is an audio briefing from Evidence Press on a research candidate about negative mutual information in time.

Start with a familiar idea. For two quantum systems at the same moment, mutual information measures how much they share, and it can never be negative.

Physicists have proposed a version for one system at two times: before and after a process. There is no ordinary joint quantum state for two times, so the proposal uses a pseudo-density matrix, an object that, unlike a quantum state, can have negative eigenvalues. Its proposers, Fullwood and Parzygnat, conjectured that this mutual information in time is never negative either. A mutual information that can go negative would be hard to read as shared information.

Fullwood and Yang proved the conjecture whenever the input is a qubit, in a preprint. The Omega Institute then published a counterexample in five dimensions, so this release is not the first counterexample. They left open the smallest size at which the conjecture fails.

This paper settles that question. A failure needs at least three input levels, at least two output levels, and a starting state that is not pure. One explicit process, with three levels in and two out, reaches all three limits at once, and its negative value is certified exactly with interval arithmetic.

A simple family of channels shows why. It is a coherent version of the textbook erasure channel, and the key is coherence between the occupied levels and an empty one. Without that coherence, for these starting states, the quantity can never be negative. At one parameter value, the sign comes down to comparing two whole numbers. Two processes that act identically on everything the system occupies can even give opposite signs.

Two questions stay open: whether the quantity can fall without limit, and how negative it can get for three-level systems. For both there is only numerical evidence.

This is an unrefereed candidate. Its checking is internal AI-assisted review and computation, not peer review. This briefing uses a synthetic voice and is not additional evidence.

relatedWorks.citation: Fullwood and Parzygnat (2025), On Dynamical Measures of Quantum Information. Entropy. Defines the dynamical mutual information from the anticommutator state over time and the signed entropy, and conjectures that it is never negative (Remark 1 and Section 5).
Wu, Parzygnat, Vedral and Fullwood (2025), Quantum mutual information in time. New Journal of Physics. Studies the same quantity under this name.

Fullwood and Yang (2026), On the entropy of a pseudo-density matrix. arXiv:2608.28946. Proves non-negativity for qubit inputs (Theorem 4.1) and supplies the block inequality used for pure inputs (Lemma 4.4(iv)); a preprint.
